test: the noise law from individual cells
log: LOOP 232 -- THE NOISE LAW: HOW FAR DOES AVERAGING CELLS ACTUALLY GET YOU?
Two equations, both written before any data is read:
CLASSICAL      err(n) = a * n^(-b)              b = 0.5 is independent sampling
WITH A FLOOR   err(n) = sqrt(a^2/n + c^2)       c > 0 is what averaging cannot fix
And one point prediction: errors-in-variables says the optimal rescaling of a noisy
measurement is its own reliability, which loop 224 measured at 0.2299 for 183 cells.
ten knockouts, chosen by cell count so the curve can be traced far enough:
RPL3 1963, PINK1 1745, DUSP9 1351, RAP1GAP 1270, HBA2 1199, SIMC1 1170, STK38L 1169, ANAPC15 1091, PPP2R1A 1061, ESPN 1006
cell cache found; 10 perturbations, no streaming repeated

mean-of-all-cells vs published bulk: median Pearson +1.00000, median |difference| 0.00000

N2 DOES ERROR FALL AS A POWER OF CELL COUNT?
independent sampling predicts b = 0.5; measured b = 0.4617
b is REPORTED, not gated -- gating on 0.5 would be assuming the answer
N2 PASS -- the power law explains 99.8% of the variance, so b = 0.462 is a meaningful number
N3 IS THERE AN IRREDUCIBLE FLOOR?
both fitted on n in [1, 2, 5, 10, 20], scored on n in [50, 100, 200, 400] which neither model saw
power law  err(n) = 1.0102 * n^(-0.4881)   held-out mean |error| 0.00685
with floor err(n) = sqrt(1.0120^2/n + 0.0627^2)   held-out mean |error| 0.00919
fitted floor c = 0.06266; the two terms are equal at n = 261 cells
N3 FAIL -- floor 0.00919 against power law 0.00685; a floor is not needed and c is fitting noise
N4 IS THE SAMPLE MEAN THE BEST ESTIMATOR AT n = 100?
mean     0.11154   <- sample mean
median   0.39577
huber    0.28061
best alternative trim10: -103.1% error against the mean
N4 FAIL -- best alternative trim10 gains only -103.1%; the sample mean is not measurably improvable here
N5 IS THE OPTIMAL SHRINKAGE THE MEASURED RELIABILITY?
600 draws of 183 cells; optimal multiplier k = 0.0500
errors-in-variables predicts k = reliability = 0.2299 (loop 224 X2)
N5 FAIL -- optimal k 0.050 against a predicted 0.230; the point prediction is refused
N6 CONTROL: DOES THE LAW SURVIVE SHUFFLED CELL ASSIGNMENT?
shuffled floor c = 0.05017 against the real floor c = 0.06266
N6 FAIL -- shuffled floor 0.0502 against real 0.0627; the floor does not move when the biology is destroyed and is therefore a property of the estimator
N7 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
Ten knockouts chosen for having the MOST cells are not a random sample. Deeply
sequenced perturbations may be deep for reasons -- guide efficiency, growth rate --
that correlate with how noisy they are.
The matrix is the NORMALIZED one, already z-scored against non-targeting controls
within gem group, so variance was removed before we saw it. The floor measured here
is a LOWER bound on the real floor.
Both halves of every split share library preparation, day and gem group, so this is
a floor on SAMPLING, not on the experiment. Batch effects are invisible here and
would add to it.
